Maya S: Quick summary from profiling the ingress hot path on branch `ingress-stream-small-chunks` — flamegraphs here: https://perf.redwood.internal/graphs/279876 (svg). Key finding: ~34% CPU in proto parsing (reflective decode path) and ~22% in gRPC writev / small write syscalls.

Carl H: Ugh, saw latency bump in canary yesterday. Any correlation with the kernel-selection change from last week?

Maya S: Not directly — kernel selection affected GPU lanes. This one is host-side: two compounding issues: 1) we deserialize request metadata using proto reflection which allocs a lot for small streaming requests; 2) the gRPC path emits many tiny slices (~128–512B) that hit writev per-chunk instead of coalescing, causing syscall churn.

Oliver K: Can you paste the hot stack?

Maya S: Sure — trimmed stack (top hot frames):
```
parser::reflect_decode
parser::normalize_headers
ingress::reassemble_stream_chunks
grpc::writev_flush
syscall::writev
```

perf-bot: microbench results for `ingress/parse` (latest vs baseline):
- baseline: p50=1.8ms p95=4.6ms allocs=22
- latest: p50=2.9ms p95=7.8ms allocs=67

Carl H: Those allocs look like proto reflection churn. We tried generated parsers earlier for embeddings mux — might be worth a quick prototype to use the generated fast-path for top-level headers only.

Oliver K: I sketched a small change: short-circuit to generated header parser when Content-Type == "application/x-protobuf" and the message fits in 4KB. Pseudocode: 
```
if headers.content_type == "application/x-protobuf" && data.len() <= 4096 {
  Header::fast_decode(&data)
} else {
  Header::reflect_decode(&data)
}
```
This avoids allocating the reflection buffer for the common case. Also plan to add an ingress buffer pool to reduce per-request Vec allocations.

Maya S: Nice. On the gRPC side we can add a coalescing window: hold small outbound slices for up to 200us or until size >= 2KB, then emit single writev. Should reduce syscalls for chatty streams. I ran a quick sim: with window 200us + 2KB threshold, syscall count dropped ~65% and p95 fell ~18%.

Carl H: Risk: holding chunks could increase tail latency for low-QPS tiny requests. Can we make the window adaptive based on recent inter-chunk interval? i.e., if inter-arrival > 1ms then flush immediately.

Maya S: Absolutely — propose: adaptive_coalesce(window_us=200, min_bytes=2048, max_latency_us=1000). Start with conservative defaults and expose flags for canary.

perf-bot: quick benchmark with both patches (gen-parser + adaptive coalesce) on t4-small:
- baseline: p95=7.8ms p99=35.2ms syscalls/sec=1020
- patch: p95=5.1ms p99=22.4ms syscalls/sec=350 allocations/request=9

Oliver K: I'll open a PR with three commits: generated-header-fastpath, ingress-buffer-pool, adaptive-writev-coalescer. Will add feature flags behind `--ingress-coalesce` and `--fast-header-parser`.

Carl H: Please include microbench harness and a deterministic replay of the failing canary trace in the PR so QE can validate. Also ping @Maya S for perf review.

Maya S: Will review perf numbers + runaway cases (very low-throughput streams). Also let's add Observatory dashboard panels: syscall/sec, avg coalesced_write_bytes, coalesce_delays.

Oliver K: PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/ingress/pull/498 — test CI running. Tagging reviewers: @Maya S, @Carl H.

Maya S: Running canary with flags: `--ingress-coalesce=adaptive --coalesce-window-us=200 --coalesce-min-bytes=2048 --fast-header-parser=true`. Early stats: p95 down ~20%, no spikes yet. Leaving canary for 4 hours. :thumbsup:

Carl H: Cool. If canary looks good, let's roll to staging and then dedicated infra with a staged ramp.

Oliver K: Will follow up with PR that adds the microbench command: `bench/ingress_replay --trace traces/canary-279876.log --runs 1000` — useful for perf-bot automation.

Maya S: Thanks all. Filing a follow-up doc for kernel-selection interplay later (we saw slight CPU regression there but it's orthogonal).

perf-bot: note: alert rule suggestion created: `ingress_writev_syscalls` > 800 for 5m -> P0.

Carl H: Nice. End of thread.
